problem_type: Canvas result lifecycle loses durable version order or deletes files before undo history can restore them
symptom: Undoing an older result deletion after a later canvas action can restore metadata that points to a file already deleted; legacy projects can also label an older current pointer as the newest version.
direct_cause: Pending file deletions were not tied to the undo journal step that created them, and legacy version normalization enumerated the current pointer before durable history order.
class_root: Result identity, durable history order, and physical-file deletion timing were not enforced at their shared lifecycle boundaries.
affected_population: Projects with generated asset files and undo history eviction
Legacy projects whose result pointer differs from history order
Loaded and closed-project deletion entry points
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an application-owned canvas journal and project persistence lifecycle; no third-party behavior decides it.
invariants: A pending file deletion is released by undo eviction only when the eviction reaches the journal generation and position that created it.
Physical deletion never occurs while any live canvas result still references the relative path.
Legacy version numbers follow durable history order, with newest entry numbered 1 and current prepended only when absent.

door_reduction.why_not: Deletion has asset-library, node-card, project-close, app-exit, queue, and flush doors; journal and lifecycle have independent readers and writers. They converge on the changed shared boundaries but cannot be removed without changing separate user and persistence flows.

generality_proof: Every loaded deletion queues through deleteAssetResult and records the current journal generation/position; the only history eviction callback supplies the exact eviction boundary. Every legacy canvas snapshot passes through normalizeNodeResultVersionNumbers, so pointer order cannot change numbering.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Attach pending physical-file deletion to the undo generation and position, and flush only eligible evicted records.
Report the generation and journal position removed by history eviction.
Normalize legacy result numbers from durable history order.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Asset library deletion calls the shared deletion boundary.
Node card deletion calls the same shared boundary.
Project release remains an explicit all-pending flush and does not rely on undo eviction.
App/project close remains an explicit all-pending flush.
All result outcomes converge on nodeRunOutcomePatch; version allocation for new results is an existing forward path outside legacy backfill.

recurrence.reason: The same deletion can be followed by any later gesture until the bounded undo journal evicts its step, and any legacy project can load with a current pointer that differs from history order.
same_class_scan: rg normalizeNodeResultVersionNumbers across canvas snapshot loading
rg deleteAssetResult across asset library and node card entry points

prevention.invariant: Only pending deletions whose own journal generation and position were evicted are eligible during an eviction callback; explicit close flushes remain comprehensive.
prevention.failure_mode: A pending record without a matching eviction remains queued, and a live reference prevents physical deletion.
prevention.strategy: Carry lifecycle metadata with the pending record and pass the exact eviction boundary from the journal owner. Normalize legacy ordering at the sole snapshot lifecycle boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old behaviors are replaced in place at the same shared boundaries; no standalone legacy production path remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the lifecycle invariant.

migration: Existing pending records are in-memory only and disappear on restart; closed-project and app-exit explicit flushes remain unchanged. Legacy snapshots are normalized on load without changing result identity or current selection.
residual_risks: A process crash before explicit close cleanup can leave an unreferenced generated file until a future startup cleanup path is added.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Deletion timing is enforced at the pending-file queue boundary; legacy ordering is normalized by the shared lifecycle model and covered by its class tests.
